beats.formula: V=integral_0^1 integral_0^1 (x+y) dif x dif y
beats.text: A double integral accumulates tiny contributions over a region in two input dimensions. For the surface z equals x plus y above the unit square, each small base rectangle contributes its area times the surface height.

Integrate one coordinate at a time. During the inner integration with respect to x, y stays constant. The result is one half plus y, representing the cross-sectional accumulation for each fixed value of the outer coordinate.

Now add those cross-sectional accumulations over y from zero to one. One half y plus one half y squared increases by one. Continuity on this rectangle justifies the iterated integration and also permits reversing the order.

beats.formula: integral_0^1 integral_0^x 1 dif y dif x=frac(1,2)
beats.text: Bounds encode geometry. Over the triangle below y equals x in the unit square, the upper y bound depends on x. Integrating one over that triangle returns its area, one half; using constant square bounds would describe a different region.

practice.prompt: Evaluate ∫₀²∫₀¹(x+2y) dy dx. Show the inner integral before using the outer one.
practice.answer: The inner integral is [xy+y²]₀¹=x+1. Integrating from x=0 to 2 gives [x²/2+x]₀²=4.

practice.prompt: A rectangle has side lengths 2 and 4 with constant density 3 kg per square meter. Express its mass as a double integral and evaluate it.
Write and evaluate a double integral for the area of 0≤y≤x≤2. Explain why the upper inner bound is variable.
practice.answer: Area=∫₀²∫₀ˣ1 dy dx=∫₀²x dx=2. For each x, the vertical slice stops at y=x, so its bound changes with x.

takeaway: Integrate small contributions over a stated region; inner variables move while outer variables temporarily remain fixed.
scope: Iterated integrals over a rectangle and a triangle, with bounds tied to geometry.
title: Multiple integrals
objective: Integrate over regions using bounds, changes of variables, and Jacobians.
